region: Te Muna Valley · Martinborough, New Zealand
about: Craggy Range was founded in 1998 by businessman Terry Peabody and viticulturist Steve Smith MW, with a focus on single-vineyard wines. Its home is the Giants winery beneath Te Mata Peak in Hawke’s Bay, but in 1999 the partners also planted Te Muna Road, a large vineyard in the Te Muna Valley just outside Martinborough, at the southern tip of the North Island. The estate is held in a 1,000-year family trust, and the 2024 vintage marked its 25th harvest.

Te Muna lies along the Huangarua River on stony terraces with limestone in places, exposed to strong winds and big swings between day and night temperatures. The higher site is picked about a week after the rest of Martinborough, which keeps freshness and acidity. In the cellar, chief winemaker Ben Tombs ferments in a mix of stainless steel and French oak barriques, partly with wild yeasts, and the wine rests about five months on its lees in older and new oak before bottling, giving more texture than a typical Marlborough Sauvignon.

In the glass the winery describes a pale straw colour and a wine that is vibrant, ripe and textured: white stone fruit, passionfruit and kaffir lime on the nose, then a lively palate with deep concentration, fine steely minerality and a saline acidity. Wine Spectator picked up intense key lime and lemongrass in the 2025. Serve it cool rather than ice-cold, around 7–10°C, and it pairs naturally with oysters, shellfish and goat cheese.
